fatal_errors: The proposed LPBF route does not address the central problem of joining or reacting a refractory high-entropy alloy with Cu despite their unfavorable mixing thermodynamics.
It misses the target intervention: liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It omits selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, and formation of the W-rich passivating interlayer that stabilizes the RHEA/Cu interface.
The claimed alternating FCC/BCC structure is not supported by the cited evidence and does not reconstruct the bicontinuous RHEA-ligament/Cu-channel architecture.
The proposed comparison against arc melting cannot discriminate whether stable, millimeter-scale RHEA–Cu integration has occurred.
explanation: The hypothesis concerns additive manufacturing of a generic RHEA rather than formation of a stable RHEA–Cu composite. Although E2 supports using mixed elemental powders in LPBF to synthesize WTaMoNbV and E1 supports the general radiation resistance of a different nanocrystalline RHEA, neither establishes that LPBF overcomes positive RHEA–Cu mixing enthalpies or creates stable Cu channels and interfaces. The relevant method is liquid-metal dealloying: molten Cu preferentially replaces Ti/V-rich interdendritic regions in directionally segregated WTaVTi, leaving continuous BCC RHEA ligaments. A spontaneously formed W-rich interlayer passivates the interface and arrests further exchange, enabling a stable, directionally aligned, large-scale bicontinuous composite. The generated experiment tests LPBF versus arc melting only for microstructure and mechanical properties, not Cu incorporation, interface stability, thermal conductivity, or the selective-dealloying mechanism.
